method: apps/web/bench.html (src/bench): stress fixture (seed 1); proxy layers for edges, ring cards, ticks and streaks; the busiest second of the run looped for 8 s after a 1 s warm-up; fixed DPR per case; fresh WebGL context per case. Interval = requestAnimationFrame timestamp deltas; cpu = stage frame() time (layer updates, uploads, render call). Timer resolution 0.1 ms; values rounded to 0.1 ms. A render sanity check (lit pixels read back after warm-up) refuses to time a stage that draws nothing.

environment.browser: Claude desktop in-app browser, Chrome/152.0.7977.130 (Windows 11, x64)
environment.gpu: ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) UHD Graphics (0x0000A78B) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)
environment.machine: laptop with hybrid graphics; the browser used the integrated GPU

correction: The first two runs recorded on 2026-10-13 measured a stage that drew nothing: three.js culled every segment quad as a back face (the shader's y flip reverses the winding). Those timings were invalid and are replaced by the runs below, measured after the fix (material side: DoubleSide). litPixels shows the frames really drew.
